item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Trump Asserts Iran Wants to ‘Make a Deal’
item.summary: Iran maintains publicly that no negotiations are taking place, but Mr. Trump claimed that Iran was so near defeat that it had little choice but to talk. Still, Iranian missiles and drones struck across the region.

item.title: Investigators Seek Answers in Attacks on Jewish Sites in Europe
item.summary: Attacks on schools and property in several countries have Jewish communities on edge, amid suspicions that Iran is behind the violence.

item.title: Trump Sours on Keir Starmer Over UK’s Decision Not to Join Attacks on Iran
item.summary: President Trump once called Prime Minister Keir Starmer a friend. But Britain’s decision not to join the attacks on Iran has led to merciless mocking by the president.

item.title: How North Korea’s Kim Jong-un Is Using the Iran War to Justify His Nuclear Arsenal
item.summary: He delivered a lengthy speech at his country’s rubber-stamp Parliament, declaring that his nuclear power will shield his country from American hostility.

item.title: Take Shorter Showers: South Korea Kicks Off an Energy-Saving Drive
item.summary: President Lee Jae Myung called on the public to cooperate, likening the energy supply disruption caused by the Iran war to the Asian financial crisis and the pandemic.

item.title: High Oil and Gas Prices Could Outlast Trump’s War With Iran
item.summary: While the president has promised rapid relief, Americans could feel the financial sting of the conflict for some time after it ends.

item.title: Qatar Is Not Mediating U.S.-Iran Talks, Foreign Minister Says
item.summary: Qatar’s Foreign Ministry warned that the regional security system has been shattered, as the war has destroyed trust between Gulf countries and Iran.

item.title: Why President Trump Has a Big Oil Problem
item.summary: Our national security correspondent David E. Sanger looks at President Trump’s trouble handling retaliatory attacks by Iran that have largely choked off the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Iran’s New Security Chief Is a Hard-Line Former Guards Commander
item.summary: Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr replaces Ali Larijani, who was killed last week in an Israeli strike. He has a history of expanding the Guards’ reach into Iran’s politics.

item.title: Lebanon Expels Iranian Envoy as Rift With Tehran Deepens
item.summary: The decision by Lebanon’s foreign ministry has heightened fears of internal instability. Hezbollah, the Iranian-backed militant group and political party, was quick to condemn the move.
